weeks.title: Measurement, Vectors & Experimental Uncertainty
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do physicists turn motion and interaction into defensible quantitative evidence?
weeks.phenomenon: Two groups measure the same motion and obtain slightly different values.
weeks.lab: Measurement/video-data diagnostic; safe household objects only.
weeks.concepts: SI units; scalar; vector; uncertainty; graph; model
weeks.reading: Course safety charter and motion dataset.

weeks.title: Position, Displacement & Velocity
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does a reference frame change how motion is described?
weeks.phenomenon: A passenger can be at rest relative to a train and moving relative to the ground.
weeks.lab: Walking-motion graph or video analysis in a clear safe space.
weeks.concepts: position; displacement; distance; velocity; reference frame

weeks.title: Acceleration & Velocity–Time Graphs
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can velocity change even when speed does not?
weeks.phenomenon: An object turning at constant speed is still accelerating.
weeks.lab: Motion-sensor simulation or supplied dataset.
weeks.concepts: acceleration; velocity; instantaneous; average; vector
weeks.quantitative: Slope and area relationships on motion graphs.

weeks.title: Two-Dimensional Motion & Projectiles
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can horizontal and vertical motion be analyzed separately in a model?
weeks.phenomenon: A dropped object and a horizontally launched object fall for similar times from the same height in an idealized model.
weeks.lab: Projectile simulation; no launching hard objects near people/property.
weeks.concepts: component; projectile; independence; trajectory; gravity
weeks.quantitative: Resolve vectors and analyze projectile motion algebraically.

weeks.title: Kinematics Inquiry & Model Selection
weeks.essentialQuestion: Which motion model best explains a real dataset?
weeks.phenomenon: A cart's position curve can be modeled in different ways.
weeks.lab: Video analysis or simulation; student-generated motion data if safe.
weeks.concepts: model; residual; fit; assumption; uncertainty

weeks.title: Forces & Free-Body Diagrams
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do interaction forces produce changes in motion?
weeks.phenomenon: An object can move even when net force is zero.
weeks.lab: Force-diagram analysis and low-force spring-scale simulation.
weeks.concepts: force; net force; inertia; free-body diagram; interaction

weeks.title: Newton's Laws
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do Newton's laws connect forces and acceleration?
weeks.phenomenon: The same force produces different accelerations for different masses.
weeks.lab: Low-force cart simulation or virtual lab.
weeks.concepts: Newton 1; Newton 2; Newton 3; mass; acceleration

weeks.title: Friction, Circular Motion & Constraints
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do curved paths require inward net force?
weeks.phenomenon: A car can move at constant speed but still require a net force while turning.
weeks.lab: Circular-motion simulation; no swinging heavy objects.
weeks.concepts: friction; normal force; centripetal acceleration; tension; curve

weeks.title: Gravitation & Orbital Motion
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can the same gravitational interaction explain falling and orbiting?
weeks.phenomenon: Astronauts in orbit are continuously falling without hitting Earth.
weeks.lab: Orbital simulation and inverse-square data analysis.
weeks.concepts: gravity; field; inverse square; orbit; centripetal
weeks.quantitative: Use proportional gravity/orbit models; Extended pathway algebra.
weeks.reading: NGSS orbit modeling and open gravitation text.

weeks.title: Work & Kinetic Energy
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does work connect force, displacement, and speed change?
weeks.phenomenon: The same force can transfer different energy depending on distance and direction.
weeks.lab: Ramp/cart simulation or safe low-energy object motion.
weeks.concepts: work; kinetic energy; system; transfer; joule
weeks.quantitative: W=Fd cosθ concept and KE calculations.

weeks.title: Potential Energy & Conservation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does system configuration store energy?
weeks.phenomenon: An object can gain kinetic energy while total system energy remains constant.
weeks.lab: Pendulum/ramp simulation; light safe objects only.
weeks.concepts: gravitational PE; elastic PE; conservation; system boundary
weeks.quantitative: Energy bar charts and algebraic conservation.

weeks.title: Power & Efficiency
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can two machines do the same work at different rates?
weeks.phenomenon: Two devices transfer the same energy in different times.
weeks.lab: Human-scale stair-power calculation if safe, or dataset.
weeks.concepts: power; efficiency; useful output; dissipation

weeks.title: Energy Systems & Engineering
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can energy models guide better designs?
weeks.phenomenon: A device loses useful energy through multiple pathways.
weeks.lab: Energy audit of a simple device/system; no mains-electrical disassembly.
weeks.concepts: energy transfer; thermal loss; efficiency; criterion; constraint

weeks.title: Momentum & Impulse
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why does interaction time matter during a collision?
weeks.phenomenon: A padded stop and a rigid stop can produce different peak forces for the same momentum change.
weeks.lab: Impulse simulation or soft-object demonstration.
weeks.concepts: momentum; impulse; collision; force-time graph

weeks.title: Conservation of Momentum
weeks.essentialQuestion: When is momentum conserved, and what system must be defined?
weeks.phenomenon: Two carts interact and total momentum remains nearly constant despite individual changes.
weeks.lab: Virtual cart collision or supervised low-energy carts.
weeks.concepts: system; internal force; external impulse; conservation

weeks.title: Elastic & Inelastic Collisions
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can momentum be conserved while kinetic energy changes?
weeks.phenomenon: Objects can stick together or rebound after collision.
weeks.lab: Collision simulation.
weeks.concepts: elastic; inelastic; kinetic energy; deformation

weeks.title: Center of Mass & Semester Synthesis
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do force, momentum, and energy models complement one another?
weeks.phenomenon: A complex motion can simplify when viewed through center of mass and system models.
weeks.lab: Integrated mechanics investigation or simulation.
weeks.concepts: center of mass; model choice; conservation; external force

weeks.title: Midterm Examination & Corrections
weeks.essentialQuestion: What have I mastered in mechanics and experimental reasoning?
weeks.phenomenon: A cumulative mechanical system requires multiple representations.
weeks.lab: No new lab; midterm and correction portfolio.
weeks.concepts: cumulative mechanics
weeks.quantitative: Mixed graphs, vectors, forces, energy, momentum.

weeks.title: Rotational Kinematics
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can angular quantities describe rotational motion?
weeks.phenomenon: Points on the same rotating object share angular motion but can have different linear speed.
weeks.lab: Turntable/wheel simulation; no high-speed rotation.
weeks.concepts: angle; angular velocity; angular acceleration; radius

weeks.title: Torque & Rotational Equilibrium
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why does where a force is applied matter?
weeks.phenomenon: A door opens more easily when pushed farther from the hinge.
weeks.lab: Safe lever/door-handle force reasoning; avoid loading furniture.
weeks.concepts: torque; lever arm; equilibrium; center of gravity

weeks.title: Angular Momentum
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can rotational speed change when mass distribution changes?
weeks.phenomenon: A spinning system changes rotation rate when its mass distribution changes.
weeks.lab: Simulation/video analysis; no spinning people on unstable stools.
weeks.concepts: angular momentum; moment of inertia; conservation; external torque

weeks.title: Rotational Energy & Rolling
weeks.essentialQuestion: How is energy partitioned in rolling systems?
weeks.phenomenon: A rolling object has both translational and rotational kinetic energy.
weeks.lab: Ramp simulation using safe lightweight objects.
weeks.concepts: rotational KE; rolling; moment of inertia; energy

weeks.title: Oscillations & Simple Harmonic Motion
weeks.essentialQuestion: What causes repeated motion around equilibrium?
weeks.phenomenon: A mass-spring or pendulum returns repeatedly toward equilibrium.
weeks.lab: Small pendulum or virtual oscillator; secure lightweight mass.
weeks.concepts: period; frequency; amplitude; restoring force; phase

weeks.title: Mechanical Waves
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do disturbances carry energy without transporting matter over long distances?
weeks.phenomenon: A pulse travels along a medium while individual points mostly oscillate locally.
weeks.lab: Rope/slinky simulation with safe spacing, or virtual wave.
weeks.concepts: wavelength; frequency; amplitude; speed; superposition

weeks.title: Sound, Resonance & Interference
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do systems respond strongly at particular frequencies?
weeks.phenomenon: Objects can resonate when driven near natural frequencies.
weeks.lab: Tone/sound simulation at safe volume; no prolonged loud exposure.
weeks.concepts: sound; resonance; standing wave; interference; decibel concept

weeks.title: Fluids: Pressure & Buoyancy
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can a heavy ship float while a small dense object sinks?
weeks.phenomenon: Floating depends on density and displaced fluid, not mass alone.
weeks.lab: Water displacement with small safe objects or simulation.
weeks.concepts: density; pressure; buoyancy; Archimedes principle

weeks.title: Fluid Flow
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do speed, pressure, and continuity interact in flowing fluids?
weeks.phenomenon: Flow changes as a tube narrows.
weeks.lab: Virtual flow lab; no pressurized systems.
weeks.concepts: continuity; flow rate; viscosity; streamline; Bernoulli concept

weeks.title: Thermal Physics & Gas Energy
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does microscopic particle motion explain temperature and heat transfer?
weeks.phenomenon: Objects at the same temperature can contain different thermal energy.
weeks.lab: Cooling-curve dataset or safe water-temperature simulation.
weeks.concepts: temperature; internal energy; heat; conduction; convection; radiation

weeks.title: Electric Charge, Fields & Potential
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can objects interact without contact?
weeks.phenomenon: Charged objects exert forces across space.
weeks.lab: Electrostatics simulation; avoid high-voltage devices.
weeks.concepts: charge; electric field; potential; Coulomb interaction; energy

weeks.title: Circuits & Electrical Energy
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do current, voltage, resistance, and power describe circuit behavior?
weeks.phenomenon: Bulbs change brightness when circuit arrangement changes.
weeks.lab: Low-voltage battery/LED/resistor lab if supervised, or circuit simulation; never use mains voltage.
weeks.concepts: current; voltage; resistance; series; parallel; power

weeks.title: Magnetism & Electromagnetic Induction
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can changing magnetic conditions produce electric effects?
weeks.phenomenon: Moving a magnet near a coil can induce a voltage.
weeks.lab: Low-voltage induction simulation or supervised coil/magnet experiment.
weeks.concepts: magnetic field; induction; flux concept; generator; motor
weeks.quantitative: Interpret induction graphs qualitatively; Extended calculations optional.

weeks.title: Electromagnetic Waves, Light & Information
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do wave principles enable imaging, communication, and energy transfer?
weeks.phenomenon: Digital signals remain usable after transmission conditions that distort analog signals.
weeks.lab: Optics/communication simulation; eye-safe light only—no lasers directed at people.
weeks.concepts: EM spectrum; photon concept; reflection; refraction; digital signal; information
weeks.quantitative: v=fλ; compare signal data and error rates.

weeks.title: Engineering Design Under Constraints
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do engineers convert a scientific problem into testable criteria and tradeoffs?
weeks.phenomenon: Two designs solve the same problem but optimize different constraints.
weeks.lab: Design challenge using paper/cardboard/simulation; no hazardous construction.
weeks.concepts: criterion; constraint; prototype; iteration; optimization; tradeoff

weeks.title: Space Systems, Remote Sensing & Climate Energy
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can physics explain orbital measurement and Earth's energy balance?
weeks.phenomenon: Satellites infer weather, surface, and atmospheric properties from electromagnetic signals.
weeks.lab: Satellite/remote-sensing dataset analysis; Solanar extension.
weeks.concepts: orbit; radiation; albedo; energy balance; remote sensing
weeks.quantitative: Orbital proportionality and incoming/outgoing energy data.
weeks.reading: Synthesis with Solanar Weather Academy and trusted satellite datasets.

weeks.title: Physics & Engineering Capstone
weeks.essentialQuestion: Can a quantitative model improve a real designed system?
weeks.phenomenon: A real problem requires mechanics, energy, waves, circuits, fluids, or sensing plus constraints.
weeks.lab: Student-designed prototype/simulation with teacher-approved safe materials.
weeks.concepts: model; prototype; test; uncertainty; optimization; communication
weeks.quantitative: At least one predictive equation/model and uncertainty analysis.

weeks.title: Comprehensive Final & Engineering Portfolio Defense
weeks.essentialQuestion: Can I integrate physics models across unfamiliar systems and defend a design with evidence?
weeks.phenomenon: A multi-system case requires representations, quantitative reasoning, and argument from evidence.
weeks.lab: No new lab; cumulative final and portfolio defense.
weeks.concepts: cumulative synthesis
weeks.quantitative: Mixed mechanics, energy, momentum, waves, fluids, circuits, data.

assessment.unit: Performance task: model + data/quantitative reasoning + CER + application/design
assessment.midterm: 15-item cumulative objective check plus corrections and portfolio review
assessment.final: 30-item cumulative objective check plus portfolio/capstone defense

safety.lab_policy: Target ≥25% hands-on/inquiry laboratory time using safe low-energy systems or supervised/virtual alternatives; no mains-voltage work.
safety.home_rule: Use only explicitly safe investigations; substitute simulation/data analysis whenever proper supervision or facilities are unavailable.
